body.statement: Determine an explicit numerical function \(\rho(n,d)\), not defined by a minimax optimization, and derive choices inside \(\mathrm{def:grouped-reconstruction-handle}\) such that \(c_\epsilon L_{n,d}\le\rho(n,d)\le C_\epsilon U_{n,d}\) and \(c_\epsilon\rho(n,d)\le R_{n,d,\epsilon}\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}E_{P^n}[W_1(\widehat G_{\mathrm{grp}},G_P)^2]\le C_\epsilon\rho(n,d)\) for every \(n\ge1\) and \(d\ge2\); the derivation must yield the exact consistency region, reproduce the \(d/n\) lower bound on the separated-atom hypercube, and give a nonconstant guarantee for two effect clusters with unknown unequal masses and propensities at both overlap boundaries.
body.justification: The open object is the full sparse-to-dense frontier, including one coherent positive estimator and a same-class all-estimator converse.
body.gap: VinayakKongKakade2019Change fixes equal trials and entity weights, LeeBacakKennedy2025 assumes smooth mixing densities with observed trial counts, and HanJiaoWeissman2018 has one-population local moments; none controls the coupled mass-weighted treated--control moment process here.
body.consumer: A solved frontier would calibrate CATE-distribution reporting for dexamethasone response profiles without claiming individual treatment effects or exact nonresponder atoms.

obligation.what_is_open: A single explicit rate \(\rho(n,d)\), a fully tuned finite version of \(\widehat G_{\mathrm{grp}}\), and a matching same-class converse in the sparse and transitional regimes remain unproved.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen assumptions permit arbitrary unknown cell masses, null cells, unequal propensities at both overlap boundaries, and tied effects.  The deterministic Lipschitz extension does not by itself control the supremum over all Lipschitz tests of the grouped factorial-moment estimation error.  The available lower families separately certify the unknown-mass and separated-atom obstructions but do not determine their sharp interpolation.
obligation.attempted: The verified route proves the global mass-weighted extension, the total empirical risk bound, a fixed-sample separated-atom hypercube lower bound, and the normalized two-categorical-sample transfer.  The grouped Jackson and factorial-moment handle was tested conceptually against these endpoints, but optimizing its joint covariance term would require a new uniform stochastic argument; summing labelwise errors only recovers the displayed empirical upper bound and cannot close the sparse logarithmic gap.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved same-class result is the explicit bracket
\[
c_\epsilon\max\!\left\{\min\!\left(1,\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\right),
\min\!\left(\frac dn,n^{-2/3}\right)\right\}
\leq R_{n,d,\epsilon}\leq C_\epsilon\min\!\left(1,\frac dn\right).
\]
The total empirical estimator attains the upper side, and the bounds match at order \(d/n\) whenever \(n\geq d^3\).  Its guarantee applies unchanged to every two-effect-cluster subfamily with unknown unequal masses and with propensities equal to either overlap boundary, giving the concrete bound \(C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/n\}\) without discarding null cells.  The separated-atom hypercube forces the matching \(d/n\) cost in the dense regime.  The bracket also implies the stated sufficient and necessary consistency boundaries and the exact bounded-category parametric-risk boundary.
